# Stage 1: Build the amg2023 application
# Using Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for a modern, stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables to enable non-interactive installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, Git, CA certificates, and Open MPI
# - build-essential: Provides C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make.
# - git: Required to clone the source code from the repository.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure HTTPS connections (e.g., for git).
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Provide the MPI implementation (mpicc, mpirun) and libraries.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings prevent common issues by:
# - Disabling the shared-memory (vader) and InfiniBand (openib) Byte Transfer Layers (BTLs),
#   which may not be available or can cause hangs in virtualized networks.
# - Forcing TCP communication over the primary network interface (typically eth0 in pods).
# - Disabling help message aggregation to prevent potential hangs with mpirun.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^vader,openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_orte_base_help_aggregate=0

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the latest version of the AMG benchmark source code, build it,
# install the executable to the system PATH, and clean up.
# FIX: The build is now initiated from the root 'AMG' directory. This allows the top-level
# Makefile to correctly build all required library dependencies before linking the final executable,
# resolving the 'cannot find -l...' linker errors.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git && \
    cd AMG && \
    # Compile the application from the root directory to build all dependencies first.
    make && \
    # Copy the final executable from its output location to a directory on the default system PATH.
    # This makes 'amg' directly available to the user.
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize the final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /root

# Define the default command. The user will typically override this with
# 'mpirun' to launch the parallel application.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 amg -n 100 100 100
CMD ["amg", "--help"]

#
# MiniCluster manifest for running the AMG benchmark on a single AWS CPU instance.
# This configuration is for a small-scale test run.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster experiment.
  name: amg2023-aws-cpu-test
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of application tasks (e.g., MPI ranks) to run across the MiniCluster.
  # Since size is 1, all 4 tasks will run on the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

  # If set to false, the pods and services are not deleted after the job completes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # List of containers to run in the MiniCluster.
  # Only one container is defined as per the requirements.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command that will be wrapped by 'flux run'.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 on a small 4x4x4 grid for testing.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
      # This container is not the designated launcher process. The Flux Operator
      # will handle the launch within the Flux instance.
      launcher: false

manager.name: Build and Deploy AMG2023
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details: Clone the latest branch of amg2023. You MUST put amg on the PATH.

context.optimize:
Maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. You MUST maximize memory per CPU core. More cores are better.
The trick to optimizing this is THREADING. You MUST force OpenMP and any math libraries to use only one thread per MPI rank. On example is setting OMP_NUM_THREADS to "1". You might also consider setting OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism to "cma" as a conservative builder will set to none.
YOU MUST SLOWLY increase the problem size, one dimension at a time, by an increment no more than double the current to increase the FOM. A timeout may not require a smaller problem size but rather a different instance.
A previous run example that has worked well:
  amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 128 -P 8 4 1 on m7g.16xlarge with FOM 8.039496e+08
The size of the MiniCluster MUST be 1. Tasks MUST be at least 4.
To reduce noise in logging, you can set logging.quiet to true.
context.resources:
The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types, and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your choice. You are still limited to one node.      
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
  hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6in.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  r7iz.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6g.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  t3a.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, AMD
